topics.topic: Exact backup encryption, authentication, metadata binding, and key-digest format
questions: What exact authenticated-encryption construction and key-digest construction must every release use, including nonce generation, key encoding or derivation, algorithm/version identification and failure handling?

Can the unencrypted record be altered independently, or must authentication bind it to the encrypted payload so that altered metadata is unreadable or invalid for listing, retention and restore checks?
What exact authenticated-encryption and key-derivation construction defines a valid encrypted backup?
How is the key digest computed, encoded and authenticated, and is equality of this value the authoritative way to select a restore key?
What exact authenticated backup format and cryptographic rules must every implementation use, including whether the clear metadata is authenticated and how the recorded key digest is computed?

quotes:
Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its
   making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about backup encryption, authentication, metadata binding, nonce handling and key-digest construction.

precedent.topic: Backup encryption, authentication, key digest, nonce, and metadata binding
quotes: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
precedent.why: The algorithm, nonce, authenticated envelope, key identifier and cryptographic-version representation are encoding and file-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Representation of M11 OwnerSession temporal facts
questions: Are M11's temporal facts UTC instants as State 1 specifies, or monotonic-clock readings as changed A13 specifies?
Are these M11 facts UTC instants, opaque monotonic-clock readings, or paired values containing both?
Are M11's session-time facts monotonic-clock readings or UTC instants, and must State 1 stop describing them as instants?

quotes:
An owner session is never
   recorded (M11), so its instants — when it began, its last request, when
   its confirmation was shown — and its expiry at the latest are held as
   readings of that monotonic clock, and only they decide its limits; the
   UTC rule for recorded times does not reach them.
judgement.why: A13 explicitly defines these temporary OwnerSession values as monotonic-clock readings rather than recorded UTC instants.

topics.topic: Semantic, canonical, and authenticated validity rules for backup records
questions: Which parseable but nonsensical values make the record invalid—for example a future or non-UTC instant, a negative sequence number, an unknown release, a digest of the wrong algorithm or length, or metadata inconsistent with the kept filename?
Does validity mean only syntactic decoding, or must the record also pass range, canonical-encoding and cryptographic-authenticity checks before it affects scheduling, retention and the owner view?
Must Registry authenticate the unencrypted record before using it for scheduling, retention deletion, naming the newest backup or choosing its age, and what happens when authentication fails?

quotes: a kept file's record is valid when its instant, release, last sequence number and key digest can all be read, and only a valid one counts as a kept backup;

It
   records, readable without its key, its instant, the release that made it,
   the last audit sequence number its store ever wrote — kept apart from the
   entries (A15), 0 for a store that never wrote one, whatever the log now
   holds — and a digest of the key it was
   made with (never the key); its age is counted from that instant.
judgement.why: Canonical encodings, field ranges, metadata authentication and the validity grammar of the backup record are file-format and schema contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Outcome when expiry cleanup races an already-admitted owner request
questions: If a request passes the session check but has not yet taken the required locks when the limit pass reaches the session, may the pass delete state that the admitted request still needs?

If a request passes the session check but has not yet acquired the import or session lock when the expiry pass acquires them and ends the session, must that admitted request still complete, or is it refused because its session state has been dropped?

quotes:
An owner
   request is any request to the owner interface that
   carries the valid session, whatever its answer; its arrival restarts the 30
   minutes — of concurrent requests the latest arrival counts; before the
   first request it runs from the sign-in.

Validity is
   checked when a request arrives (A04 rule 6, stage 1); a request that
   passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs, and
   a restart that interrupts it leaves nothing of it (A04 rule 4).
judgement.why: This is the same unchanged race between expiry cleanup and a request already admitted at arrival.

precedent.topic: Outcome when expiry cleanup races a previously admitted owner request
quotes:
An owner
   request is any request to the owner interface that
   carries the valid session, whatever its answer; its arrival restarts the 30
   minutes — of concurrent requests the latest arrival counts; before the
   first request it runs from the sign-in.

Validity is
   checked when a request arrives (A04 rule 6, stage 1); a request that
   passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs, and
   a restart that interrupts it leaves nothing of it (A04 rule 4).
precedent.why: Validity and idle renewal are explicitly decided at request arrival, so a request arriving before the limit remains admitted even if a sweep later obtains the lock.

topics.topic: Required controls and verification for encryption at rest
questions: What concrete host controls satisfy this requirement, and what evidence or verification closes it if Registry performs no check?
Is encryption at rest merely an external deployment precondition with no verifiable Registry guarantee, or must some deployment evidence or start-time check establish it?

quotes:
The store, the backup location and the disks under them are encrypted and
   kept out of VM Agent's reach by the owner's administration of VM Platform
   (R0-48; Explicit exclusions); Registry does not check the host.
judgement.why: The text expressly makes encryption at rest an external host-administration obligation and states that Registry performs no verification.

topics.topic: Timing, overlap, and missed-interval behavior of the 60-second expiry pass
questions: Are passes fixed-rate or fixed-delay, may they overlap, and after missed intervals does Registry run one pass immediately, run several catch-up passes, or wait for the next interval?
When is the first pass, and what happens when a pass is delayed or lasts across a later 60-second boundary?

quotes:
Registry
   ends it — and drops its pending confirmation and its uploaded file with it
   (M11) — at a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the
   start; the pass alone ends sessions by their limits, taking the import
   lock and then each session's lock (A16 rule 2) and deciding under them.

A session that has reached a limit serves no request from that
   moment: a request carrying it is refused at the session check.
judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about the expiry pass's phase, cadence and treatment of delayed or missed passes.

precedent.topic: Expiry-pass initial phase, cadence, and handling of missed passes
quotes:
Registry
   ends it — and drops its pending confirmation and its uploaded file with it
   (M11) — at a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the
   start; the pass alone ends sessions by their limits, taking the import
   lock and then each session's lock (A16 rule 2) and deciding under them.

A session that has reached a limit serves no request from that
   moment: a request carrying it is refused at the session check.
precedent.why: The limits themselves determine request refusal exactly, so the first tick, delayed-tick policy and overlap handling affect only internal reclamation of already inaccessible session state.

topics.topic: Whether a scheduled date skipped by an overlapping run can run later
questions: After the earlier run finishes, is that date permanently marked as missed, or may a later clock look start its backup late?
Is a date skipped because another backup run overlaps its 03:00 permanently missed by that process, or may it run if the wall clock is later set back and crosses that date's 03:00 again?

quotes:
a date's
   run starts at its first look at or after 03:00 of that date when an
   earlier look of the same process saw that date before 03:00, and no kept
   backup of that date exists

Runs
   never overlap: a 03:00 that finds a run still going makes no run of its
   own.
judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about whether a date skipped because another run overlaps its qualifying time can run later.

precedent.topic: Whether an overlapping backup run permanently skips the next eligible date
quotes:
a date's
   run starts at its first look at or after 03:00 of that date when an
   earlier look of the same process saw that date before 03:00, and no kept
   backup of that date exists

Runs
   never overlap: a 03:00 that finds a run still going makes no run of its
   own.
precedent.why: Only the date's first qualifying look can start its run, and if that look finds another run active the date makes no run of its own, so it is skipped rather than started later.

topics.topic: Deletion order and failure behavior for temporary-file cleanup
questions: In what order are temporary files removed, determining which files remain when one deletion fails?

topics.topic: Event that determines a refused-sign-in timestamp
questions: At what monotonic event is a refusal timestamped for counting and for the start of the fifth-refusal lockout?

topics.topic: Event that determines an owner request's arrival timestamp
questions: Which event fixes the monotonic arrival reading: receipt by the HTTP server, beginning the handler, completion of authentication, or acquisition of the session lock?

topics.topic: Exact backup filenames, prefixes, and collision prevention
questions: What exact names identify Registry backup files and prevent two backups with distinct recorded instants from colliding?

topics.topic: Import-lock scope during a session-limit pass
questions: Does one pass hold the import lock while it visits every session, or release and reacquire it separately for each session?

topics.topic: Required ordering outcome for concurrent correct and wrong sign-ins
questions: When four refusals already exist and a correct and a wrong sign-in arrive concurrently, must the correct sign-in succeed and clear the count, must the wrong one trigger lockout first, or may either serial outcome occur?

topics.topic: Required suspension-aware monotonic clock capability and startup behavior
questions: How must Registry establish that its clock counts both host and VM suspension, and what happens at start if the runtime or hypervisor cannot provide that guarantee?

topics.topic: Retention and enforcement requirements for old backup keys
questions: Must old backup keys remain available while any kept backup names them, and where is that requirement enforced or recorded?

topics.topic: Whether backup metadata must be confidential without the backup key
questions: Does “cannot be read” apply only to the encrypted store payload, or must the metadata also be unavailable without the key?
